reviews.comment: I love this guy even though I got a B. For an intro class that I took as a senior, very easy. However, don't blow off the little assignments and pay attention to the syllabus grading categories. Something may be worth 5 pts but can count a lot more because it's in a different grading category. Lots of extra credit, critical thinking on exams!

If you go to class, you will get an A in this class. His lectures at times can be repetitive, but is very passionate about his job. If you miss any in-class assignments, it will be hard to get a good grade because it's 40%. Tests are written on lecture topics, media watched in class, and textbook definitions.

Nice guy, but I wouldn't take him again. His lectures are boring and half the time I was wondering what any of it even had to do with sociology. 3 exams, no final, a few outside of class assignments, but mostly in class participations. If you skip class, you will probably fail. Also doesn't put his slides on canvas, which is annoying.

Professor Woods is an AMAZING guy! You can tell he truly cares for his students and cares for Sociology. If it was just him I truly would have no problem with this class. Unfortunately everything is graded by his TA... and she was not helpful whatsoever. She gave little to no feedback on our written assignments, truly the least helpful TA I've seen

Dr. Woods is a good instructor, but he doesn't post lecture slides, so attendance is a must. All assignments are done & submitted in class (40% of grade). There are three exams (20% each) based on both lectures and the textbook (divided~60/40) so you have to read it. He makes this intro class approachable and enjoyable with popculture references.

Dr. Woods is a nice guy. Attendance for grade only on certain days. The class is lecture heavy which he can only do so much about. PAPERS EVERY WEEK, the papers are terrible very confusing and the rubric doesn't help much but it is the base of how you'll be graded. TA does all the grading, and mine personally SCREWED me in this class!!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very, very, kind and caring professor. I did take him in a class of about 20 people but I know he does do larger class sizes. TAKE HIM! There are a few random grades and then three tests plus a video project. He is lecture heavy so go to class but attendance isn't mandatory. He gives grandpa core but in an energetic way. Overall amazing prof.
He was a great professor! The class wasn't super hard as long as you paid attention and took notes because he doesn't post the slides. He was super nice and pretty flexible

Dr Woods was an amazing professor. Get involved in the lectures and participate in class and you will have no problem passing his class. It can be difficult if you miss lectures because he doesn't post slides but overall he is a great professor.

I won't be going into soci, but I can say that I really enjoyed Dr. Wood's class. His lectures were entertaining and he had insightful things to say. He was into class engagement. Personable guy, and he is also passionate about giving back to the community; he gives outlets for his students to do the same. Easy A if you somewhat pay attention.
Woods is super nice and willing to answer questions. Great teacher overall.

Professor woods was great! this class was a writing intensive course so there are 6 total papers which are short and the same prompt for every paper. They can be difficult because of how much reading is involved and the TA graded everything. Overall easy course but need to attend class for info and he does have some in class mini assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The prof overall was great, the TA's is what makes the class hard. The weekly papers were graded harshly by the TA, if you didn't have exactly what they wanted then you'd fail. Prof was knowledgeable about the course.

Woods is both kind and respectful towards his students through his lectors. He's a great professor and definitely enjoys what he teaches. His exams are open note and are based on subjects talked about in class as well as some subjects in the textbook. Most of the homework assignments were graded by the TA whom can be strict in their gradings.

Amazing professor, 3 exams all online and open note, exam questions from slides and a few from textbook, a few easy assignments, grade can change a lot from one grade, easy going guy that loves sociology

Professor Woods is very passionate about what he teaches and makes this class enjoyable. The essays are graded by his TAs. The grading can seem harsh at first, so make sure you talk with the Tas about what they are looking for and they are happy to help.

This is my second time having professor Woods and I would recommend taking him a million times over. He is really passionate about sociology and wants his students to succeed. Most of the grades were papers that were graded by the TAs. Class wasn't too difficult if you show up to lectures and get feedback from the professor and TAs.

Soci major. Love his class! 205 for soci majors only is very easy! Great class, really engaging and Woods truly cares. Attendance is not mandatory, but the test covers material from his PowerPoints in class. 3 Tests, not cumulative, open note & book, online, take-at-home, not proctored. Several assignments and group work. Nice TA and fair grading.

Dr. Woods is a good professor, but the 230 class can be a bit boring at times. If you go to class and don't procrastinate the papers and final project it's not that bad. Also, the papers are graded by the TA.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I honestly loved having him as a professor! The class was a writing-intensive course so there were a lot of papers but they were easy. There's no tests and attendance was not really mandatory. The TA's grade your papers but his lectures are pretty helpful. He seems to really care about what he's teaching and tries to make his lectures interesting!
reviews.ratingTags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is def an underrated professor. I genuinely love this man as a professor, he's very passionate about the topic and is a very kind person. At least for SOCI majors, the textbook was required for small assignments, but not everyday reading.

Best professor I have had at A&M. Dr. Woods is super kind and willing to help students whenever needed. He keeps his lectures entertaining and is not a tough grader as long as you put in the work. Highly recommend. I have taken two classes with him and he is one of my favorite professors!

Woods is rad! For SOCI 230, it really depends on your TA since they will be the ones grading the papers, but Woods is awesome for lectures. This is my second time taking a class of his and I definitely would again. He is funny, cares about getting to know you, and is helpful in talking to you about your college journey/future career. He's great.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was so enjoyable and Dr. Woods plays a huge role in that. His lectures are very interesting and there are no tests. His papers are very simple as you keep doing more. Our final paper is graded very easily and can bring your grade up a whole letter grade. I would take him again.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr woods is great. TA is such a hard grader. Should be an A but whatever. help

he doesn't post his slides online so you have to show up to lectures but he is an amazing professor. his lectures prepare you really well for his exams which are are open note and take home. his engagement assignments are straightforward and theres some group work. overall, pretty easy class and chill prof.

the most mid class i have ever taken. i get that intro classes are meant to lack more interesting concepts but this class was more boring than ever. i would've enjoyed this class much more if it wasn't for the professor. i felt like he was in my personal space & put his hands on my desk area and i felt very uncomfortable by it. pls take some1 else

Professor Woods was amazing. He has a lot of assignments to help boost your grade and the exams were easy, online, and open note. He loves to engage with students during lectures where a lot of the exam material comes from. Be sure to show up to class and take notes. I highly recommend taking this class with this professor.

He should have a much higher rating! He is funny, has great flowing lectures, and is easy to talk to if you need help on anything. You take his tests online and they are open to everything. No posted lectures, but that is so you can be engaged in conversations, group activities, and much more. If you have to take this course take HIM!
very nice his class is pretty easy. take home tests and very few assignments
Overall a good lecturer. Six critical analysis papers, friday breakout assignments, and the term paper are what make up your grade. The workload was very doable. I would definitely take him again!

Dr. Woods is such a caring professor and he really knows what he's talking about. It's important to attend his class because he does not post slides. This class is basically writing a bunch of papers over theorists, but you only need to write 6 so very flexible. Graded by TAs tho. If you have Charlene as your TA then you're set. Just follow rubric!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Woods is the BEST. Absolutely take his class if you have the chance. He is so genuine & cares about his students deeply. He doesn't take attendance, but the things discussed in lecture are on the exams. There is 3 exams & no final, but all of our exams were open note & taken at home. He offers service project as extra credit!
I loved this class, just be prepared to be in class every Friday for your breakout assignments.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a simple class to pass/get a good grade in as long as you attend class and pay attention to what he is saying. The tests are on both things in the lectures and information in the textbook so it would be in your best interest to look at both when studying. He is willing to talk things through if anything happens. Plenty of volunteer hours.
Dr Woods is such a sweet guy and he really is passionate about his work. He's an amazing professors and wants his students to succeed and think outside of the box. Take him!
Participation matters, he regularly calls on students to answer questions. Very likeable person and cares a lot about his students.

This is hand down one of my favorite professors at A&M. NO EXAMS just essays and some easy in-class assignments every Friday. The class was structured very well and clearly. I would highly recommend going in for feedback after your first essay overall an easy class if you are willing to do the work. don't skip and ask questions during lectures!!!
Professor Woods's lectures are good and sometimes can be entertaining. TA's usually grade the papers, make sure to follow the rubric and you'll get a good grade.

I don't recommend buying the textbook for Soc 230. Instead, only do the papers where he provides readings on canvas. For the remaining papers email the TA for a copy. Another hint... choose the readings that are not popular. The TA doesn't know all the readings well and grades easier on Dubois/Caso vs a popular guy like Karl Marx or Emile.

Soci 230 is graded by TA's. I like Wood's and think he is a great lecturer. I don't know how he grades tho, because TA's grade the course. My one complaint however is that when defining key concepts they expect you to magically know their specific list terms instead of reader interpretation. I find that very unfair as how can I guess what you think

Dr. Woods is an AMAZING professor and made class super interesting. Due to covid, the volunteering is optional for extra credit to drop your lowest test grade but honestly it was super fun going to volunteer and you really get to connect with the class. His tests were easy and straightforward. Go to his lectures because questions are on the test.

Professor Woods is so nice and makes class as interesting as possible. Gives reviews for tests and clear outlines for papers. I would definitely recommend him and will try to take more of his courses!!
he is the least helpful professor on the planet. do yourself a favor and take someone else
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He mumbles when he speaks, he doesn't respond to your emails, and he is very vague during lectures while also being very specific during exams. I wouldn't recommend him at all

TAKE Professor Woods for 230 it was great! The first critical analysis paper I received a low score but I made the effort to go speak to the TA and before every single critical analysis paper I would have the TA read over it and give me feedback. Also I hate public speaking but I was prepared so it was totally fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Woods is an ok prof. The class consists of 2 test and the final is an e-portfolio over the service hours. My class had to do 10 hours of community service, you got to choose the place but it had to be approved by him. He doesn't post his lectures so you have to go to class to get the notes and the tests are over the lectures
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Woods isn't bad at all. Take notes on the lecture and the textbook chapters for the tests and you'll do fine. There are only two tests which are fairly easy if you study and then the "final" is a portfolio which isn't too bad either. His lectures can be boring, but he gives useful information. Overall, I'd recommend him for this intro class :)
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tim Woods is a good prof, he's pretty boring in class but there isn't a lot of homework. The exams are not real difficult, and the required community service and project is actually fun and doable to get an A which is a big percent of your grade. I would recommend if you don't mind reading the book bc I learned more from the book than the lectures.

I loved this class and Professor Woods. Easily my favorite teacher. He is caring about his students especially if you go to his office hours. Community service is a requirement and is fun. I would take this class again if i could.
Great Professor. Learned a lot. Take him.

I took him for 230 and 430 was a bit more difficult, but the exact same format. 6 critical analysis papers due over the sem, one group presentation and a term paper. it's harder since they're contemporary sociologists but still a solid choice for the class!
Great prof. Understanding and helpful.
You're required to do community service for his class. Tests are a little difficult but not too bad. Community service was the only real drawback for this class.

Hes a great professor! This is a really boring class but he really enjoys what he lectures on. Each week you have a critical analysis due but you only have to do 6 the whole year. They arent bad. Theres a final term paper that isnt bad either as long as you dont wait too long! Attending class isnt mandatory but I always went
reviews.ratingTags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Woods is very straightforward with his grading and will not accept any late papers unless it is excused by the university. There were many who didn't bother going to class but his lectures will help you write your papers for good grading. There is a term paper for which I advice to not leave it for last minute, which is based on your interest
reviews.ratingTags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Good guy but very blunt. Lectures are straightforward and attendance is necessary. Writing intensive so weekly papers due (easy) plus a 7 page term paper, which sounds terrible but it honestly is not difficult. Overall a decent professor!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Great class by a great Prof. No exams, but plenty of papers. Am taking him again in the spring.
Great Prof.  Do the work and you get an A or B.   Interesting projects and lecture.  Learned a lot.

He was terrible. I was fairly involved in class but when I answered questions he made me feel bad/stupid for answering HIS questions!! I started skipping his class due to frustration with him and my grade in his class slipped from a 'B' to an 'F'. (I got low B's on the 2 tests given in the class but received a 60 on the project). Avoid taking him!!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are good, but all over the place. The stuff he talks about in class shows up on the test so go to class. The service project is cool to do and get in the community, but do NOT leave it to the last minute.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Good prof. Doesn't post lectures online so don't skip class if you want an A. You must read the book for tests as well as know the lecture material- if you do this it isn't too bad. Has a service project worth 40% of your grade which is very time consuming but awesome opportunity. Not an easy A but it is possible. Would recommend!!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best professor ever.   Cool lectures and much of grade based on hands-on service-learning assignment.

Most interesting lectures I must say. But if you're one of those people who cannot memorize stuff, then you're definitely not getting an A in this class. Assignments are due by the end of the semester. Also, u need to complete 10 hours of community service and make an audio and video presentation on that.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy to understand and very passionate about his subject!

Absolutely amazing. Cares about you paying attention, and tries to keep class engaged and interested. Very funny. Tests are over things covered in lecture and in the textbook. 5/5 since I overslept the final and he let me take it during office hours - a real lifesaver.

I loved taking Dr Wood's class! I chose option 1 in his class where I took two tests and volunteered. To get an A on his tests go to lecture and take detailed notes, READ the textbook and take notes as well. Study that and you are ready for an A. The volunteering journals are easy and you get great feedback if you submit them on time!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I've taken so far. Really interesting material. Recently redesigned this class. Two different options: Service Learning which requires students to do 10-15 service hours, but tests are weighted less, with a final portfolio being worth 40% of your grade. The other option is the traditional exams and in class participation activities.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr Woods. I did the service learning and was able to offset my test average (average of 81% between the two tests) with the project and still make an A. His voice is very interesting to listen to and not monotone which helps make lectures easier to listen to. If you do not volunteer you grade is 3 major exams. I do recommend him!

He makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Like it's possible to do the bare minimum and pass, but you won't make an A. For each test, you pretty much have to read the textbook or you wont do well. His lectures don't cover much of the material you get tested over, and he speaks really softly, so don't sit in the back.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Woods was a great professor. It was not an easy class but he is willing to help if you go to office hours.  He is a very intelligent man and knows what he is talking about. I would recommend him to anyone!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Woods is a nice guy and makes class interesting. He responds quickly to emails and if you go to office hours he's always willing to help. The lack of extra credit and outside work makes this class not so easy if you don't do well on the first test. Make sure you read the text and readings if you want to do good. Don't take if you want an easy A
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: he gives 2 options: volunteer and keep a journal, or take the class like a normal class with an extra short answer question on each test. He asks a lot of questions and does in class activities instead of straight lectures, which aren't hard but are kinda boring. You need to read the textbook and the Massey reader (if you're the second option)
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a very good instructor. I felt like I was actually learning in his class. He does a really good job of interacting with the class, giving good power points, and showing visual aids. Also, he gives the option to get 50% of your grade from volunteering. Definitely recommend him.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super sweet person however he is a tough grader and expects a lot from you. Heavy focus on discussion based on the readings for the class, and there were a lot of readings Tests are written ONLY and somewhat hard, unless you can memorize a whole essay for the exam since he gives you a bank of questions beforehand and picks a few to put on exams.

I highly recommend not taking this professor. He is unclear with what he wants on his papers, and is a very tough grader. His exams are essay exams with 4-5 essay questions, that he does not prepare the students for in any way.

I had Woods for 205 and 489. Yes there is a lot of reading, but it is a college class some of them will require reading. He will always help if you make the effort. He responds to emails usually within 24 hours even over breaks. If you don't understand something just ask. Make sure to pay attention to videos he asks about those on tests!
One of the best at A&M.  Highly recommend you take him.

I found Dr Woods to be a great teacher.   He is very kind and has a straightforward way of teaching.   I met with him several times during office hours and he helped me every time.   He cares about students that care about learning.

Professor Woods is not evil! His syllabus was clear cut, his lectures, while sometimes running into each other, were clear as well. I will say, if you don't want to go to class, don't sign up for this class. If you don't want to stay on top of readings, don't sign up. This class takes consistent effort. On another note, there's only one paper.
Don't take his class, my only advice. I struggled throughout the whole semester and even went to office hours all the time. It barely helped, and the tests are pretty hard. Do not take him!

Passing Woods class depends mostly on all of the outside readings. You will not pass if you do not read and take notes over what you are reading. Attendance is mandatory, but I constantly fell asleep in class and seriously didn't miss much. The paper is easy to do if you ask the TA for clarification, and tests are confusing but passable.
Top notch professor.   High expectations, but that's what I am paying for.  If your looking for an easy class, go elsewhere.  If you want to learn, take this class.
Every rating on here is 100% accurate to the way Professor Woods conducts his class. I would not advise anyone to take a class with him.

His lectures are long and scattered. He can't give you definite answers to your questions and does not explain why you are wrong, just says you are wrong. There is a lot of reading. The tests are ridiculously hard, even when going to class and reading. He was a complete jerk to me when I met with him one on one too. Would not recommend him.

This guy is an absolute jerk, at least in my experience. Went to him for help multiple times and he blew me off, canceled meetings and ignored my emails. In lecture he is not really clear at all and he talks very quietly so if you sit in the back chances are you won't hear him. He's boring, doesn't lecture clear info, and grades unnecessarily hard

There was way too much outside reading for a 3 hour course, his tests also cover such minute details, there is only one outside paper so I guess that was a plus. Don't expect him to curve the class at all, even if you just need a point

I fell in love with sociology but not with him. He does not curve at all even though his class is way harder than neccessary. cannot believe i got a B after working so hard; cannot believe a class like this could have brought down my GPA. do not recommend. sociology is great but he is not.

I worked very hard (didn't miss a single class, read every reading and textbook chapter, and extensively studied every term and concept possible) and made a B in this course (my only B, I'll add). Tests are confusing and did not seem to reflect the textbook or what he had been teaching us. He's nice but made sociology way harder than necessary.

As a professor, he sucked. The lectures are three times a week and many times seem to go over little information. Although, the lectures are interesting it gets to a point it feels like they are wasting your time. Tests are challenging because of his lack of teaching and preparation for them and mainly material from lecture (book is a supplement)

DO NOT TAKE. Lectures are scattered. Tests are hard. Grades the paper really hard. The lecture material is what most of the test is based off of, but you have to know the material much deeper than what he gives you. The book doesn't explain the lecture material well. And he doesn't put his lectures online. He's a nice guy, but it's not worth it.

Took attendance and sometimes gives participatory grades in class. YOU MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK & SUPPLEMENTAL MASSEY READINGS TO DO WELL ON THE EXAMS. There's one paper - many of my classmates got C's but I got an A+ so I guess it depends?  Doesn't always give straight answer if you ask for clarification. Lots of discussion  group work in class.
The only plus about this class was there's no homework but 3 exams w a final and short essays that were graded very harshly. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND. Oh, and you WILL NOT PASS IF YOU DO NOT READ.

Dr. Woods is a nice guy but the class is a lot more challenging than expected. His lectures normally take the entire time and cover a lot of information. Participation is needed to do well and you have to attend class if you want to do well. The material isn't really hard but the test are kinda tricky and require studying if you want to do well.
Hard and boring class.

Dr. Woods is a great guy, but his class was pretty difficult. He is not clear on what is going to be on the exams and his lectures can be a bit scattered. The class was definitely a lot harder than it should have been. You MUST read in order to do well on the exams and the chapters are fairly long and kinda boring. 3 exams and 2 short papers.

Not a very hard subject, just a hard class because there are not very many grades. Grades papers harder than they should be graded. His TA's are not very helpful at all. Not very clear on what will be on the tests.  I would not recommend this class.

Dr. Woods is the sweetest guy ever! He is very funny in his lectures, and makes me want to hug him. Haha. Made a B solely because I didn't study much. Two essays, they were graded fairly tough. Definitely my favorite class of the semester and I'm going to miss it. Take him!

I took Soci 205 with Dr. Woods at TAMU and it was fairly easy. He does random participation points, so you almost always need to be in class, because they are worth a fair amount.  All of his tests are straight from the notes and the final was NOT cumulative. I would definitely recommend  re-take Dr. Woods.

I only missed his class once but never once opened the book and I usually B's on his tests and papers. I know quite a few people who struggled with this class but I'd say if you pay attention to the lectures (and they're interesting anyway) you should do fairly well on the tests and papers. 3 exams, 2 papers, the 3rd exam counts as the final.

Woods is a good professor but the one thing that makes the class hard is that he talks very quite.  This makes it hard to understand him so make sure to sit close. Reading is essential and the chapters are long, his lectures are okay and they are on slideshows but they can be very confusing and with the amount of reading combined it makes it hard.
Extremely little homework, tests are definition based and not hard if you take about 2 hours out of your day to study.

Going to lecture makes a major difference in how well you understand the material. He bases his test off of things discussed in class, and even some of the videos we watched.  Final is not cumulative and there are two papers during the semester. If you do well on the first one, you can use your grade for the second. Lecture is interesting and funny
